ai.literal: Firmness in action is called a person's firmness of mind; all other things are different.
ai.translation: What is called firmness in action is in truth a person's firmness of mind; all other external assets are of a different, lesser nature.
ai.modern: செயல் உறுதி என்று சொல்லப்படுவது ஒருவனுடைய மன உறுதியே ஆகும்; மற்றவை எல்லாம் அதற்கு வேறானவை.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true source of strength required to accomplish any task. The poet states that 'vinai-t-tiṭpam' (resoluteness in action) is nothing other than 'mana-t-tiṭpam' (resoluteness of mind). Without an unwavering mind, no external resources, wealth, or planning can bring success. All other external aids are secondary and do not constitute true, reliable strength.

ai.literal: Avoiding obstacles, after they occur not flinching, the way of these two, they say, those who analyzed, is the principle.
ai.translation: To avoid actions that bring ruin, and to remain undaunted if an obstacle does occur—those who have deeply analyzed action say that the path of these two is the core principle.
ai.modern: துன்பம் தரும் செயல்களைத் தவிர்ப்பதும், துன்பம் வந்தபோது தளராமல் இருப்பதும் ஆகிய இவ்விரண்டின் வழியே சிறந்த கொள்கை என்று ஆராய்ந்தவர்கள் கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core of resolution in action through two complementary practices. First, one must avoid ('ஒரால்') undertakings that lead to ruin or harm ('ஊறு'). Second, if obstacles do inevitably arise, one must not flinch or lose heart ('ஒல்காமை'). Those who have deeply analyzed the nature of successful action ('ஆய்ந்தவர்') state that mastering these two paths ('இவ்விரண்டின் ஆறு') is the ultimate principle ('கோள்') of achievement.

ai.literal: To do that which is fit to be done so as to be revealed only at the end is strength of character; if it is revealed in the middle, it will bring irreparable distress.
ai.translation: True determination lies in performing an action so that it is revealed only upon completion; if the secret leaks out midway, it will bring irreparable ruin.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலை அது முடியும் வரை வெளியே தெரியாமல் செய்து முடிப்பதே ஆண்மையாகும்; அது நடுவிலேயே வெளிப்பட்டுவிட்டால், அது நீக்க முடியாத பெரும் துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of maintaining secrecy and focus when executing a plan. True strength of character, or 'āṇmai', is shown when a person carries out a necessary task in such a way that it is only made public at the very end. If the plans or actions are revealed prematurely in the middle of execution, it will lead to failure and bring about irreparable ruin. Thus, confidentiality and quiet execution are vital components of resolute action.

ai.literal: Saying is easy for anyone; doing in the manner spoken is difficult.
ai.translation: To speak of an action is easy for anyone; but to perform it exactly as spoken is difficult.
ai.modern: சொல்லுவது எல்லாருக்கும் எளிதானது; ஆனால் சொல்லியபடியே அதைச் செய்து முடிப்பது கடினமானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the contrast between speech and action, which is central to the power of action (வினைத்திட்பம்). Anyone can easily boast or lay out plans in words. However, translating those words into actual deeds and executing them exactly as promised is a rare and difficult feat. The poet uses the simple contrast between 'எளிய' (easy) and 'அரிய' (difficult) to emphasize that true strength lies in execution, not in mere talk.

ai.literal: Greatness having attained, those who are excellent, their firmness in action, with the king, impact having attained, will be esteemed.
ai.translation: The firmness in action of those who have attained greatness and excellence will reach the ruler, yield successful results, and be highly esteemed.
ai.modern: பெருமை பெற்றுச் சிறந்தவர்களுடைய செயல் உறுதியானது, அரசனிடத்துச் சென்று பயனைத் தந்து, எல்லாராலும் மதிக்கப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how unwavering determination in action is recognized and valued. When individuals of noble character and excellence (maṇṭār) possess firmness in action (vinaittiṭpam), their resolve does not go unnoticed. It reaches the attention of the ruler (vēntankaṇ) and produces tangible, successful results (ūṟu). Consequently, their strength of purpose is highly praised and esteemed (uḷḷappaṭum) by the sovereign and society alike.

ai.literal: Those things planned, in the very manner planned, they will attain, those who planned, if they possess to be firm-minded.
ai.translation: Those who have planned an action will achieve exactly what they planned, in the very way they intended, if they possess firmness of mind.
ai.modern: எண்ணியவர்கள் மனவலிமை உடையவர்களாக இருக்கப் பெற்றால், அவர்கள் எண்ணியவற்றை எண்ணியவாறே அடைவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of determination and firmness of mind in achieving one's goals. The poet states that if those who plan a task possess unwavering resolve, they will achieve exactly what they intended, in the precise manner they envisioned it. The repetition of the root word for thinking highlights the direct connection between the initial plan and the final achievement. The condition of being firm-minded is presented as the ultimate key that turns thoughts into reality.

ai.literal: Having seen the appearance, not despising is necessary; for the rolling big chariot, those who are like the axle-pin, it has.
ai.translation: One should not despise others by looking at their appearance; for even a mighty rolling chariot has those who are like its small axle-pin.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய தோற்றத்தைக் கண்டு அவரை இகழக் கூடாது; உருண்டோடும் பெரிய தேருக்கு அச்சாணி போன்றவர்கள் இவ்வுலகில் இருக்கிறார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises us never to underestimate or mock anyone based solely on their physical size or outward appearance. To illustrate this, it uses the metaphor of a massive, rolling chariot. Though the chariot is grand and powerful, it cannot move or function without its tiny axle-pin. Similarly, there are individuals who may seem small or insignificant in appearance, but they possess the essential strength and capability to hold great tasks together.

ai.literal: Without being confused, in the action determined, without wavering, delay having discarded, to perform.
ai.translation: Perform the action that has been clearly decided without any confusion, doing so without faltering and discarding all delay.
ai.modern: மனக்குழப்பம் இல்லாமல் ஆராய்ந்து முடிவு செய்த செயலை, சோர்வடையாமல், காலந்தாழ்த்துதலை நீக்கிச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the ideal execution of a chosen task. First, the action must be decided upon 'without confusion' (kalankātu kaṇṭa). Once decided, one must perform it 'without faltering' (tuḷaṅkātu) or wavering in resolve. Finally, the poet emphasizes 'discarding delay' (tūkkam kaṭintu), as procrastination can ruin even the best-planned efforts. The key words 'kalankātu' (unconfused) and 'tuḷaṅkātu' (unfaltering) show the progression from mental clarity to physical steadfastness.

ai.literal: Even if suffering comes intensely, do, having strengthened determination, the action that yields happiness.
ai.translation: Even if it brings intense suffering at first, one should carry out with firm determination any action that will ultimately yield happiness.
ai.modern: முடிவில் இன்பத்தைத் தரும் செயலை, தொடக்கத்தில் மிகுந்த துன்பமே வந்தாலும், மன உறுதியோடு செய்து முடிக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of perseverance and long-term vision in action. The author advises that when an action is known to yield ultimate happiness or success, one must not abandon it due to temporary hardships. Even if intense suffering ('tuṉpam uṟa') arises during the process, one must summon inner strength and determination ('tuṇivu āṟṟi') to complete the task ('ceyka viṉai'). The focus is on enduring short-term pain for long-term gain.

ai.literal: Whatever other firmness even when attained, those who do not possess firmness in action, the world will not value.
ai.translation: Even if they possess every other kind of strength, the world will not respect those who lack firmness in action.
ai.modern: எவ்வளவு வலிமைகளைப் பெற்றிருந்த போதிலும், செய்யும் செயலில் உறுதி இல்லாதவர்களை இந்த உலகம் மதிக்காது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of resoluteness in action. The term 'enait-tiṭpam' refers to any other kind of strength, such as wealth, physical power, or intellectual capacity. The poet asserts that even if one attains all these other strengths, they are of no value if one lacks 'vinai-tiṭpam', which is firmness and determination in executing a task. The world will ultimately disregard and fail to respect those who cannot carry out their actions with unwavering resolve.
